exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: without is a preposition taking saying goodbye as its object; the whole phrase without saying goodbye then describes how he left.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: on governs the whole clause what you need rather than one word; the clause is its object, and on what you need completes depends.

rules: A noun phrase or pronoun after a preposition is its object; together they form a prepositional phrase.
A gerund phrase can serve as object of a preposition.
An interrogative clause can also be the object of a preposition.

questions.question: What is me in beside me?
questions.correct: me is governed by beside.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: me is governed by beside.

questions.question: Why is saying used after without?
questions.correct: without is a preposition taking a gerund phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: without is a preposition taking a gerund phrase.

questions.question: What is what you need after on?
questions.correct: The whole clause is governed by on.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The whole clause is governed by on.

narration.text:
介词像一个关系箭头，但箭头后面必须有落点。这个落点就是介词宾语；介词和它的宾语合在一起，才构成完整的介词短语。<#0.8#>
She sat beside me。<#0.8#>beside 表示旁边的关系，me 是这个关系指向的对象，所以 me 是介词宾语。beside me 整块再去说明 sat 的位置，不能把 me 当成 sat 的直接宾语。<#0.8#>
He left without saying goodbye。<#0.8#>without 后面没有接普通名词，而是 saying goodbye。它表示“说再见这件事”，整块动名词短语受 without 支配，仍然是介词宾语。<#0.8#>
The choice depends on what you need。<#0.8#>on 后面的落点更长，是 what you need 这个从句。先把从句完整框起来，再判断它整体受 on 支配；不要跳进从句内部，把其中某一个词单独当介词宾语。<#0.8#>
判断方法很直接：先圈介词，再找它后面管到哪里。落点可能是代词、动名词短语，也可能是从句；边界不同，形式不同，但它们承担的都是介词宾语这一任务。

course.title: Predicatives
course.meta: Identifying or describing the subject
examples: Amy is a doctor.
The soup tastes delicious.
The problem is that we lack time.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: is does not express an action by Amy; it links Amy with the identity a doctor, making a doctor the predicative.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: tastes means “has a taste” here, and delicious describes soup; it refers back to the subject rather than receiving an action.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The whole clause that we lack time states what the problem is and fills the predicative slot after is.

rules: A predicative follows a linking verb and identifies or describes the subject.
Sensory and change-of-state linking verbs also take predicatives, not action objects.
A noun, adjective, prepositional phrase, non-finite structure or clause may serve as predicative.

questions.question: What element is a doctor?
questions.correct: is links the subject to its identity rather than expressing an action.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: is links the subject to its identity rather than expressing an action.

questions.question: Why is delicious not an object?
questions.correct: tastes is linking; delicious describes soup.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: tastes is linking; delicious describes soup.

questions.question: What is that we lack time as a whole?
questions.correct: It follows is and states what the problem is.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It follows is and states what the problem is.

narration.text:
看到 is、tastes 这类词，先别急着问“动作碰到了谁”。有时它们只是搭一座桥，把主语和它的身份或状态连起来；桥后面的部分，才叫表语。<#0.8#>
Amy is a doctor。<#0.8#>is 在这里没有表示一个具体动作，而是把 Amy 和 a doctor 连起来。a doctor 说明 Amy 的身份，所以是表语，也可以理解为对主语的补充说明。<#0.8#>
The soup tastes delicious。<#0.8#>tastes 不是说汤主动品尝了什么，而是在表达汤尝起来的状态。delicious 回头说明 The soup 怎么样，因此它是表语，不是宾语。<#0.8#>
The problem is that we lack time。<#0.8#>这次 is 后面不是一个词，而是 that we lack time 整个从句。它把问题的具体内容说完整，所以整个从句作表语。<#0.8#>
辨认表语时，先看动词是否在表示身份、性质、状态或变化，再看后面的内容能否回指主语。能回答主语“是什么、怎么样”的，就是表语；即使它是一整句话，也要按完整边界分析。

course.title: Object complements
course.meta: Completing the description of the object
examples: They elected Mia captain.
The news made us happy.
I saw him cross the road.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Mia is the object of elected, and captain gives Mia an identity; since “Mia is captain”, captain is the object complement.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: made first affects us, and happy states the resulting state of us; it complements the object rather than describing the action’s manner.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: him is the object of saw and the understood subject of cross; cross the road states what he did, so it is an object complement.

rules: An object complement forms an object + identity/state relation with the object.
An adjective can be an object complement describing the object’s resulting or perceived state.
An infinitive or participle can be an object complement describing an action done or undergone by the object.

questions.question: Whom does captain describe?
questions.correct: Mia = captain, so captain is an object complement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Mia = captain, so captain is an object complement.

questions.question: What element is happy?
questions.correct: happy describes the state of us.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: happy describes the state of us.

questions.question: How does cross the road relate to him?

options.text: It states the action done by him
It modifies the manner of saw

questions.correct: him is the understood subject of cross.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: him is the understood subject of cross.

narration.text:
有时动词后面已经有宾语，但意思还没说完，还要再补一句“这个宾语是谁、怎么样，或者做了什么”。这块补充内容就是宾语补足语。<#0.8#>
They elected Mia captain。<#0.8#>Mia 是 elected 的宾语，captain 说明 Mia 被选成什么。Mia 和 captain 之间能建立“她就是队长”的关系，所以 captain 是宾语补足语。<#0.8#>
The news made us happy。<#0.8#>us 是受到影响的对象，happy 描写 us 产生的状态。happy 不是动作方式，也不是另一个宾语，而是把宾语的状态补完整。<#0.8#>
I saw him cross the road。<#0.8#>him 是 saw 的宾语，cross the road 说明 him 做了什么。这里要把宾语和后面的动作联系起来，不能把 cross 误当成全句第二个限定谓语。<#0.8#>
检查宾补可以在宾语和后面内容之间加入“是、变得、做了”来理解。如果后半部分正好补充宾语的身份、状态或动作，而且动词需要这层信息才能完整，就应分析为宾语补足语。

course.title: Pre- and postmodifiers
course.meta: Modifiers describe nouns; position depends on structure
examples: The red school bus stopped.
The girl with a red scarf is Mia.
The book that you lent me is useful.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: bus is the head of the subject noun phrase; The limits reference, while red and school describe colour and purpose before the head.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: with a red scarf follows girl and answers “which girl”, so it is a postmodifier; the whole noun phrase is the subject.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: that you lent me follows book to identify which book and is a postmodifier as a whole; inside the clause, that is also the direct object of lent.

rules: A single adjective, determiner or noun modifier normally precedes the head noun.
A prepositional phrase or longer non-finite modifier normally follows the head noun.
A relative clause follows its antecedent, and the relative word has a role inside the clause.

questions.question: What is red in red school bus?
questions.correct: red precedes and modifies the head bus.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: red precedes and modifies the head bus.

questions.question: What does with a red scarf modify?
questions.correct: It follows girl and answers “which girl”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It follows girl and answers “which girl”.

questions.question: What is that you lent me as a whole?
questions.correct: The whole relative clause modifies book.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The whole relative clause modifies book.

narration.text:
定语的任务是帮助听者认出“哪一个人或东西”。短的修饰常放在名词前，较长的短语或从句常放在名词后，但它们都围绕名词工作。<#0.8#>
The red school bus stopped。<#0.8#>整句先看主干：The red school bus 是主语，stopped 是谓语。red 和 school 都放在中心词 bus 前，帮助说明是哪一辆车，因此属于前置定语。<#0.8#>
The girl with a red scarf is Mia。<#0.8#>with a red scarf 紧跟 girl，说明是哪一个女孩，所以整块介词短语作后置定语。is Mia 才是主干的谓语和表语。<#0.8#>
The book that you lent me is useful。<#0.8#>that you lent me 也是放在 book 后面限定它，只不过这次修饰部分是一整个从句。外层主语要一直框到从句结束，is useful 才接着构成主干。<#0.8#>
判断定语先找中心名词，再问旁边内容是否在回答“哪一个、什么样的”。不要只根据长短判断；关键是它修饰名词，而不是说明动作发生的时间、地点或方式。

course.title: Time, place and frequency adverbials
course.meta: When, where and how often
examples: We met after class.
They play football in the park.
She has often visited us.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The skeleton We met is complete; after class only adds when the meeting happened, so it is a time adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: football is the object of play; in the park answers “where”, not “what”, so it is a place adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: has visited is the verb phrase; often appears after the first auxiliary has and states how frequently the visiting happens.

rules: A time adverbial gives a point, period or duration and has relatively flexible position.
A place adverbial gives the location of an action or state and often follows the verb and object.
Frequency adverbs normally precede a lexical verb, follow be, or follow the first auxiliary.

questions.question: What question does after class answer?
questions.correct: It gives the time of met.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It gives the time of met.

questions.question: What is in the park?
questions.correct: It modifies play and gives its location.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It modifies play and gives its location.

questions.question: Where does often normally go in a perfect construction?
questions.correct: A frequency adverb normally follows the first auxiliary.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A frequency adverb normally follows the first auxiliary.

narration.text:
状语是在主干之外补充动作背景的成分。这一节只看三个最常用的问题：什么时候、在哪里、多久或多常发生。<#0.8#>
We met after class。<#0.8#>主干 We met 已经完整，after class 只是回答什么时候见面，所以整块是时间状语。去掉它，句子仍有主谓骨架，只是时间信息少了。<#0.8#>
They play football in the park。<#0.8#>play 直接带 football 作宾语，in the park 回答在哪里踢球，因此是地点状语。它修饰的是 play 这个动作，不是限定 football。<#0.8#>
She has often visited us。<#0.8#>often 表示动作出现的频率。这里 has 和 visited 共同组成谓语动词组，频率副词放在第一个助动词 has 后面。它的位置受英语谓语结构影响，不能机械照搬中文顺序。<#0.8#>
判断时先拿出主干，再对剩余内容提问：回答何时的是时间状语，回答何地的是地点状语，说明动作出现次数或规律的是频率状语。同时还要看它究竟修饰动词，还是紧跟名词去限定名词。

course.title: Manner, degree and scope adverbials
course.meta: How, to what degree and over what scope
examples: Mia answered the question carefully.
The water is very cold.
Only Mia solved the problem.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: the question is the object of answered, while carefully answers “how” and functions separately as a manner adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: cold is the predicative describing water; very sits next to cold and raises its degree, so it is a degree adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The position of only gives it scope over Mia: it means “Mia alone”, so Only Mia fills the subject slot while only focuses Mia internally.

rules: A manner adverbial says how an action happens and normally follows the verb’s object.
A degree adverbial modifies an adjective, adverb or certain verb and normally stays close to it.
The position of focus adverbials such as only, also and even changes their scope and meaning.

questions.question: What does carefully most directly modify?
questions.correct: It gives the manner of answering.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It gives the manner of answering.

questions.question: What does very modify?
questions.correct: very gives the degree of cold.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: very gives the degree of cold.

questions.question: What does Only Mia solved the problem emphasize?

options.text: Mia only solved rather than checked

questions.correct: only is adjacent to Mia, so its scope is the subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: only is adjacent to Mia, so its scope is the subject.

narration.text:
同样是状语，有的说明动作怎样进行，有的说明程度高低，还有的只把重点框在某一部分。判断时要先找它真正影响的对象。<#0.8#>
Mia answered the question carefully。<#0.8#>主干里 answered 带 the question 作宾语，carefully 回答“怎样回答”，所以是方式状语。它说明动作的进行方式，不是形容 the question。<#0.8#>
The water is very cold。<#0.8#>is 连接 The water 和 cold，cold 是表语。very 紧贴 cold，只把“冷”的程度往上推，因此是程度状语。它修饰形容词，不直接修饰 is。<#0.8#>
Only Mia solved the problem。<#0.8#>only 靠近 Mia，作用范围就是主语，意思重点落在“只有 Mia”。如果只看到它是副词，却不看位置和范围，就会漏掉句子的真正强调。<#0.8#>
分析这类状语，可以问三个问题：它在说明动作怎么做，还是把性质推到什么程度，还是把重点限制在哪一块。先找修饰对象，再给状语分类，比背固定位置更可靠。

course.title: Cause, purpose and result adverbials
course.meta: Why, for what aim, and with what result
examples: Because of the rain, the match stopped.
She left early to catch the bus.
He was so tired that he fell asleep.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: the match stopped is the skeleton; Because of the rain answers why it stopped, so the whole prepositional phrase is a cause adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: left is the predicate verb and early is a time adverbial; to catch the bus states the intended goal and is a separate purpose adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: so tired gives the degree, and that he fell asleep states the actual consequence; the whole that-clause is a result adverbial.

rules: A cause adverbial answers why and may be a phrase, non-finite structure or clause.
A purpose adverbial states an intended goal, often with to do, in order to or a so that clause.
A result adverbial states an actual consequence, often with so...that, such...that or only to do.

questions.question: What relation does Because of the rain express?
questions.correct: It states why the match stopped.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It states why the match stopped.

questions.question: What kind of adverbial is to catch the bus?
questions.correct: It states the intended goal of leaving early.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It states the intended goal of leaving early.

questions.question: What does that he fell asleep express?
questions.correct: Falling asleep is the consequence of being tired.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Falling asleep is the consequence of being tired.

narration.text:
原因、目的和结果都能给动作补充逻辑，但方向不同：原因在回答为什么发生，目的在回答想达到什么，结果在回答最后实际发生了什么。<#0.8#>
Because of the rain, the match stopped。<#0.8#>the match stopped 是发生的事，Because of the rain 把停止的原因放在前面，所以它是原因状语。<#0.8#>
She left early to catch the bus。<#0.8#>left 是已经做出的动作，to catch the bus 说明提前离开的目标。赶上车是她想实现的事，不是句子已经确认出现的结果，因此是目的状语。<#0.8#>
He was so tired that he fell asleep。<#0.8#>so 把 tired 的程度推高，that he fell asleep 说出由此真正产生的后果。睡着不是预先要完成的目标，而是太累带来的结果，所以整个从句作结果状语。<#0.8#>
区分时按时间方向想：动作之前促成它的是原因，动作时心里瞄准的是目的，动作或状态之后实际出现的是结果。不要只看到某个连接形式就下结论，要回到句中逻辑。

course.title: Condition, concession and comment adverbials
course.meta: Condition, counter-expectation and speaker stance
examples: If you hurry, you can catch the train.
Although it was cold, they swam.
Fortunately, everyone arrived safely.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: If you hurry supplies the condition under which can catch the train is true, so the whole if-clause is a condition adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Although it was cold concedes the cold, yet the main clause says they still swam; this counter-expectation makes it a concession adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: everyone arrived safely states the event; Fortunately evaluates the whole event, so it is a sentence-level comment adverbial.

rules: A condition adverbial states what the main clause depends on.
A concession adverbial acknowledges a fact while the main result counters expectation.
A comment adverbial expresses the speaker’s judgment or attitude toward the whole clause.

questions.question: How does If you hurry relate to the main clause?
questions.correct: Hurrying is the condition for catching the train.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Hurrying is the condition for catching the train.

questions.question: What does Although it was cold express?
questions.correct: Cold would normally prevent swimming, yet they went.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Cold would normally prevent swimming, yet they went.

questions.question: What is the scope of Fortunately?
questions.correct: It evaluates the whole proposition that everyone arrived safely.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It evaluates the whole proposition that everyone arrived safely.

narration.text:
有些状语不是补充时间地点，而是在搭建整句话的逻辑背景：事情在什么条件下成立，结果是否出乎预期，或者说话人怎样看待这件事。<#0.8#>
If you hurry, you can catch the train。<#0.8#>后半句能否实现，要看前面的 If you hurry 是否满足，所以这个从句是条件状语。它提供的是主句成立的前提。<#0.8#>
Although it was cold, they swam。<#0.8#>冷通常会让人不去游泳，但实际结果是 they swam。前面先承认事实，后面却出现反预期结果，因此这是让步关系。<#0.8#>
Fortunately, everyone arrived safely。<#0.8#>Fortunately 不是说明怎样到达；怎样到达由 safely 表达。它是在评价“大家安全到达”这整件事，传达说话人的庆幸，所以是评注性状语。<#0.8#>
判断这三类时看作用范围：控制主句能否成立的是条件，承认阻碍却不改变结果的是让步，表达说话人态度并评价整句的是评注。

course.title: Apposition
course.meta: A second expression identifying the same referent
examples: Mr Li, our English teacher, is speaking.
Paris, the capital of France, attracts tourists.
The news that we won is true.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Mr Li and our English teacher refer to the same person; the latter is not another subject but an appositive renaming the former.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Paris and the capital of France name the same place; commas show that the latter adds information rather than identifying which Paris.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: that we won supplies the content of news and stands in apposition to it; that has no subject or object role inside the clause.

rules: An appositive refers to the same entity as the preceding noun and renames or explains it.
A non-restrictive appositive adds extra information and is normally set off by commas.
An appositive that-clause gives the content of an abstract noun; that has no role inside it.

questions.question: How does our English teacher relate to Mr Li?
questions.correct: Both expressions refer to the same person.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Both expressions refer to the same person.

questions.question: Why is the capital of France set off by commas?
questions.correct: The core Paris attracts tourists remains complete without it.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The core Paris attracts tourists remains complete without it.

questions.question: What does that we won specify?
questions.correct: The clause states what the news is.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The clause states what the news is.

narration.text:
同位语可以理解成：同一个人或事物，紧接着换一种叫法再说明一次。前后两块指向同一个对象，不是一个修饰另一个的普通性质。<#0.8#>
Mr Li, our English teacher, is speaking。<#0.8#>Mr Li 和 our English teacher 都指同一个人。后者告诉我们李老师的身份，因此作同位语；拿掉这块附加说明，主干仍然成立。<#0.8#>
Paris, the capital of France, attracts tourists。<#0.8#>Paris 与 the capital of France 也是两个名称指向同一座城市。逗号把附加解释隔开，主干是 Paris 作主语，attracts 作谓语，tourists 作宾语。<#0.8#>
The news that we won is true。<#0.8#>that we won 不只是描述消息的外在特点，而是在回答消息的具体内容是什么，所以它是同位语从句。这里的 that 负责引出内容，不在从句内部充当成分。<#0.8#>
辨认同位关系，可以问前后两块能否画等号，后面是否在重命名或解释前面的内容。若只是回答“哪一个、什么样的”，则更可能是定语。

course.title: Dummy subject it
course.meta: Postponing a heavy notional subject
examples: It is important to sleep well.
It is clear that he agrees.
It took me an hour to finish.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: What is important is to sleep well; it merely fills the subject slot so the longer infinitive can remain at the end.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: clear evaluates the proposition that he agrees; it is the dummy subject, while the that-clause carries the real content.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: it fills the subject slot, while to finish names the activity that took time; me is the experiencer and an hour the duration.

rules: it can be a dummy subject with an infinitive as the postponed notional subject.
it can postpone a that subject clause to keep the opening lighter.
In It takes + person + time + to do, it is dummy and the infinitive is the notional subject.

questions.question: What is to sleep well semantically?
questions.correct: important evaluates the act of sleeping well.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: important evaluates the act of sleeping well.

questions.question: What function does that he agrees have?
questions.correct: The clause supplies what is clear.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The clause supplies what is clear.

questions.question: What is the notional subject in It took me an hour to finish?
questions.correct: it fills the position; to finish names the actual event.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: it fills the position; to finish names the actual event.

narration.text:
英语不喜欢把很长的主语全堆在句首，常先让 it 占住主语位置，再把真正要谈的事情放到后面。这个 it 叫形式主语。<#0.8#>
It is important to sleep well。<#0.8#>important 真正评价的是 to sleep well，也就是睡好觉这件事。it 不指某个具体东西，只让句首结构轻一些；to sleep well 才是真正主语。<#0.8#>
It is clear that he agrees。<#0.8#>clear 所判断的内容由 that he agrees 给出。前面的 it 仍然只是占位，后面的整个从句是真正主语。分析时不要把 that 从句误当成普通宾语。<#0.8#>
It took me an hour to finish。<#0.8#>句首 it 继续占位，to finish 表示真正需要完成的事项。me 是经历这段时间的人，an hour 是所用时长，各有自己的位置。<#0.8#>
识别形式主语，可以检查 it 是否有明确指代，再看句末的不定式或从句是不是整句真正谈论和评价的内容。能后移长内容、自己又没有实义的 it，就是形式主语。

course.title: Dummy object it
course.meta: Using it before a heavy object
examples: I find it useful to review daily.
She made it clear that she disagreed.
We consider it necessary that everyone attend.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: find uses it to fill the object slot, useful evaluates it, and to review daily at the end supplies the real content.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: it after made is the dummy object and clear is its complement; that she disagreed is postponed to state what was made clear.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: consider places it before the complement necessary, then gives the real object in the that-clause, keeping the verb and complement together.

rules: In find/think/consider + it + adjective + to do, it is a dummy object.
In make it clear that..., it can postpone a that object clause.
The dummy-object pattern avoids placing a heavy object between the verb and its object complement.

questions.question: Does it refer to a specific thing here?

options.text: No; it fills the object position

questions.correct: What is judged useful is to review daily.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: What is judged useful is to review daily.

questions.question: What is that she disagreed?
questions.correct: The clause gives the actual content made clear.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The clause gives the actual content made clear.

questions.question: Why is it used?

options.text: To keep the verb-complement frame clear

questions.correct: The heavy clause is postponed while it fills the object slot.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The heavy clause is postponed while it fills the object slot.

narration.text:
宾语太长时，英语也会先用 it 占住宾语位置，把真正宾语放到后面。这样动词和紧跟的宾语补足语不会被一大段内容隔开。<#0.8#>
I find it useful to review daily。<#0.8#>find 后的 it 是形式宾语，useful 是宾语补足语。真正被判断为有用的是 to review daily，所以这块不定式才是真正宾语。<#0.8#>
She made it clear that she disagreed。<#0.8#>made 后先放 it，再用 clear 补充说明；clear 的具体内容由 that she disagreed 给出。it 没有指代某件物品，整个 that 从句才是真正宾语。<#0.8#>
We consider it necessary that everyone attend。<#0.8#>consider、it、necessary 先形成清楚的框架，that everyone attend 放到末尾承载实际内容。长从句后移，读者更容易看出动词与补足语的关系。<#0.8#>
判断形式宾语时，看见“动词、it、形容词、长内容”这一排列，要检查形容词真正评价谁。若评价的是后面的不定式或从句，it 只是占位，后面的长内容才是真正宾语。

course.title: Elements in existential there clauses
course.meta: Marker, existential verb and postposed subject
examples: There is a book on the desk.
There are two reasons.
Your bag is there.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: There only opens the existential construction; a book is the entity introduced as postposed subject, and on the desk gives the place.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: are does not agree with there but with the head reasons of the postposed subject; two reasons is plural, so are is used.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Here there can answer “where is the bag” and has real locative meaning; it is not the clause-initial existential marker.

rules: Existential there is a semantically empty marker, not a place adverbial.
The form of be normally agrees with the head of the postposed subject.
Existential there introduces a new entity; locative there has real reference and can be stressed.

questions.question: Which part actually expresses place?
questions.correct: there is the marker; on the desk is the place adverbial.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: there is the marker; on the desk is the place adverbial.

questions.question: There ___ two reasons.
questions.correct: The postposed subject two reasons is plural.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The postposed subject two reasons is plural.

questions.question: What is there in Your bag is there?
questions.correct: It has the locative meaning “in that place”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It has the locative meaning “in that place”.

narration.text:
there 有两种完全不同的工作：一种只负责把“有某物”带进句子，另一种真的表示“在那里”。判断时不能只看这个单词，要看整句结构。<#0.8#>
There is a book on the desk。<#0.8#>句首 There 不指具体地点，只是存在句引导词；is 是存在谓语，a book 是被介绍出来的后置主语，真正的地点由 on the desk 表达。<#0.8#>
There are two reasons。<#0.8#>这里 are 的单复数不是跟句首 There 决定，而是看后置主语 two reasons。中心词 reasons 是复数，所以使用 are。<#0.8#>
Your bag is there。<#0.8#>这次句子已经有主语 Your bag，is 后的 there 能直接回答包在哪里，也可以在口语中重读，所以它有真实地点意义，作地点状语。<#0.8#>
分辨方法是先看 there 后是否紧接存在谓语和新出现的人或物；如果是，它多半只作引导。若句子已有明确主语，there 又能回答“在哪里”，它就是有实义的地点状语。

course.title: Subject complements in passives
course.meta: Object complements becoming subject complements
examples: Mia was elected captain.
He was seen to enter the room.
The door was painted red.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: In active They elected Mia captain, captain complements Mia; once Mia becomes the passive subject, captain becomes a subject complement.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The active can be someone saw him enter; when him becomes passive subject He, to returns before enter and the infinitive is a subject complement.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: was painted is the passive predicate; red states the resulting state of subject door rather than another action, so it is a subject complement.

rules: When an active object becomes a passive subject, its object complement becomes a subject complement.
After a perception verb becomes passive, omitted infinitival to is normally restored.
A participle or adjective can also complete the subject’s state after a passive verb.

questions.question: What is captain in Mia was elected captain?
questions.correct: In active elect Mia captain, captain is the object complement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: In active elect Mia captain, captain is the object complement.

questions.question: He was seen ___ the room.
questions.correct: The passive of see restores infinitival to.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The passive of see restores infinitival to.

questions.question: What does red describe?
questions.correct: red describes the door’s resulting state.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: red describes the door’s resulting state.

narration.text:
一个人被选成队长，“队长”仍然在说明这个人，不会因为句子用了“被”就变成另一个宾语。主动句变成被动句后，原来的宾语变成主语，原来的宾补也就跟着变成主语补足语。<#0.8#>
Mia was elected captain。<#0.8#>was elected 是被动谓语，Mia 是主语。captain 说明 Mia 被选成什么，它与主语建立身份关系，因此是主语补足语，不是 elected 后的新宾语。<#0.8#>
He was seen to enter the room。<#0.8#>He 是被看见的人，to enter the room 说明主语做了什么。感官动词变为被动后，原来省略的 to 通常恢复，整块不定式作主语补足语。<#0.8#>
The door was painted red。<#0.8#>was painted 表示被漆，red 说明 The door 最后形成的状态。它不是漆的方式，而是对主语结果状态的补充。<#0.8#>
判断时追踪关系变化：先找被动主语，再看后面的名词、形容词或不定式是否仍在说明这个主语的身份、状态或动作。能补全主语意义的，就是主语补足语。

course.title: Non-finite structures as elements
course.meta: Identify the whole function before internal structure
examples: She has a report to finish tonight.
Learning a language takes time.
Seen from above, the city looks beautiful.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: to finish tonight follows report and identifies which report, so the whole phrase is a postmodifier; tonight modifies finish inside it.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Learning a language contains a verb-object relation internally, but the whole phrase names an activity and serves as subject before takes.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The understood receiver of Seen from above is the city, meaning “when viewed from above”; the whole participle phrase is a viewpoint adverbial.

rules: An infinitive can be subject, object, predicative, modifier, complement or adverbial; position and pattern determine its role.
A gerund retains verbal properties but has a noun-like function as subject, object, predicative or prepositional object.
A participle phrase can be modifier, adverbial or complement; identify its understood subject and voice relation.

questions.question: What does to finish tonight modify?
questions.correct: It identifies the report to be finished.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It identifies the report to be finished.

questions.question: What is Learning a language as a whole?
questions.correct: It precedes takes and names an activity.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It precedes takes and names an activity.

questions.question: Who is understood as being seen?
questions.correct: The city is what is seen from above.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The city is what is seen from above.

narration.text:
一句话里出现多个像动词的形式，不等于每一个都在负责全句时态。先找真正带时态的那一个，再把剩下的整块圈出来，看它在外层句子里做什么。<#0.8#>
She has a report to finish tonight。<#0.8#>全句谓语是 has。to finish tonight 紧跟 report，说明是哪一份报告，所以整块作后置定语；tonight 只在这块内部说明 finish 的时间。<#0.8#>
Learning a language takes time。<#0.8#>takes 是限定谓语，Learning a language 整体表示一项活动，放在谓语前作主语。它内部虽然有“学习”和“语言”的关系，外层任务仍是一个完整主语。<#0.8#>
Seen from above, the city looks beautiful。<#0.8#>Seen from above 表示城市从上方被看时的视角，逻辑承受者是 the city。整块分词短语修饰主句，作状语；looks 才是主句谓语。<#0.8#>
处理非谓语，记住顺序：先确认它不负责全句时态，再判断完整边界和逻辑主语，最后看它整体是主语、定语、状语还是补足语。

course.title: Clauses as sentence elements
course.meta: Bracket the clause, then identify its whole role
examples: I know why he left.
The student who answered first won.
We will start when everyone arrives.

analyses.label: Relative clause; who is its subject

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Although why he left contains “why”, it answers “what do I know”, so the whole clause is the object of know.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: who answered first as a whole modifies student; inside the clause, who is also the subject of answered.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The main clause We will start already has its skeleton; when everyone arrives only states the starting time, so it is a time adverbial clause.

rules: A nominal clause can function as subject, object, predicative or appositive.
A relative clause functions as modifier, while the relative word also has a role inside it.
An adverbial clause modifies the main predicate or whole clause and expresses time, cause, condition, concession and other relations.

questions.question: What is why he left as a whole?
questions.correct: It supplies what I know, not why I know it.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It supplies what I know, not why I know it.

questions.question: What role does who have inside the clause?
questions.correct: who links the clause and is the subject of answered.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: who links the clause and is the subject of answered.

questions.question: What is when everyone arrives as a whole?
questions.correct: It states when we will start.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It states when we will start.

narration.text:
从句里面有自己的主谓关系，但放进更大的句子后，它还会整体承担一个外层任务。分析时必须先框出从句，再分别看外层和内层。<#0.8#>
I know why he left。<#0.8#>主句是 I know，know 需要补出知道的内容。why he left 整块回答“知道什么”，所以作宾语从句；它不是在说明 I know 的原因。<#0.8#>
The student who answered first won。<#0.8#>who answered first 跟在 student 后，说明是哪一个学生，因此整个从句作后置定语。进入从句内部，who 又承担 answered 的主语，连接作用和内部成分要同时看到。<#0.8#>
We will start when everyone arrives。<#0.8#>We will start 已有完整主干，when everyone arrives 只是说明开始的时间，所以整个从句作时间状语。<#0.8#>
判断从句功能，不要只凭开头的连接词。看它在外层填了什么空：补动词内容的是宾语，限制名词的是定语，给主句添加时间等背景的是状语。

course.title: Coordination, sharing and ellipsis
course.meta: Recover parallel structure before assigning roles
examples: Mia bought books and magazines.
Tom and Mia opened the box and checked it.
Mia likes tea; Tom, coffee.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: books and magazines on both sides of and each answer “bought what”, so they are coordinated direct objects at the same level.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: Tom and Mia jointly perform both actions, so opened and checked share the subject; each predicate has its own object, the box and it.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The clauses are parallel, so the second expands to Tom likes coffee; Tom is subject and coffee is the object of the omitted likes.

rules: A coordinator joins words, phrases or clauses of equal status; analyse both sides at the same level.
Coordinated subjects may share a predicate, and coordinated predicates may share a subject.
In ellipsis, recover the shared material from the parallel item before assigning functions.

questions.question: How are books and magazines related?
questions.correct: and joins two objects at the same level.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: and joins two objects at the same level.

questions.question: Who is the subject of checked it?
questions.correct: The second predicate omits the repeated subject and shares it with opened.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The second predicate omits the repeated subject and shares it with opened.

questions.question: What is omitted in Tom, coffee?
questions.correct: Parallelism recovers Tom likes coffee.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Parallelism recovers Tom likes coffee.

narration.text:
并列结构会把同一层级的内容放在一起，有时还会共享主语、谓语，甚至省掉重复部分。分析前先还原平行关系，再给每块命名。<#0.8#>
Mia bought books and magazines。<#0.8#>books 和 magazines 都回答买了什么，and 把两个直接宾语连接在同一层级。不能把 and 后面的 magazines 看成另起一句。<#0.8#>
Tom and Mia opened the box and checked it。<#0.8#>Tom and Mia 是并列主语，共同完成两个动作。opened 带 the box 作宾语，checked 带 it 作宾语；第二个动作共享前面的主语，没有必要重复写出。<#0.8#>
Mia likes tea; Tom, coffee。<#0.8#>分号两边结构平行，后一部分省略了与前面相同的谓语。还原后就能看出 Tom 是主语，coffee 是省略谓语所带的宾语。<#0.8#>
处理并列和省略，先看连接或标点两边是否地位相同，再补回能从前文确定的共同成分。还原后的结构说得通，成分判断才可靠。

course.title: Nested constituent analysis
course.meta: Work outside-in and keep levels separate
examples: The teacher said that the test was easy.
The book that you recommended is useful.
The students in the library read quietly.

analyses.label: Noun phrase with relative clause as subject

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: At the outer level, the pattern is The teacher—said—object clause; inside it is the test—was—easy, so was is not the main predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: The book that you recommended is the whole subject; inside that larger element, that you recommended only postmodifies head book.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: in the library follows students and identifies which students, so it is a postmodifier; quietly directly describes the manner of read.

rules: In a complex sentence, first locate the main finite verb, then its subject, object or predicative.
A large constituent may contain smaller ones; label its outer and inner functions separately.
When a prepositional phrase follows a noun, first test whether it modifies that noun; otherwise it may be an adverbial.

questions.question: What is the main-clause predicate verb?
questions.correct: was is inside the object clause; said is the outer predicate.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: was is inside the object clause; said is the outer predicate.

questions.question: What is the outer role of The book that you recommended?
questions.correct: The internal that-clause modifies book, while the whole noun phrase is subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The internal that-clause modifies book, while the whole noun phrase is subject.

questions.question: Why is in the library a modifier?

options.text: It gives the manner of reading

questions.correct: It immediately identifies students; quietly gives the manner of read.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It immediately identifies students; quietly gives the manner of read.

narration.text:
复杂句容易错，不是因为成分突然变多，而是不同层级叠在一起。最稳的方法是从外到内，一层一层拆，不能把内层谓语和外层谓语并排计算。<#0.8#>
The teacher said that the test was easy。<#0.8#>先看外层，The teacher 是主语，said 是主句谓语，后面整块从句作宾语。进入从句内部，the test、was、easy 才构成自己的主系表关系。<#0.8#>
The book that you recommended is useful。<#0.8#>外层主语是 The book that you recommended 整块，is 是谓语，useful 是表语。在主语内部，that you recommended 只负责修饰中心词 book。<#0.8#>
The students in the library read quietly。<#0.8#>in the library 紧跟 students，限定是哪一些学生，所以在主语内部作后置定语；quietly 才直接说明 read 的方式。<#0.8#>
做嵌套分析时，先找主句限定谓语和主干，再圈出大成分边界，最后进入大成分内部继续拆。每次只回答当前层级的问题。

course.title: Integrated constituent analysis
course.meta: Verify by boundaries, relations and substitution
examples: My brother Tom sent me a photo yesterday.
The young scientist explained the result to us clearly.
She saw the man with a telescope.

analyses.label: Object with a potentially ambiguous postmodifier

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: First take the skeleton My brother Tom—sent—me—a photo; then read Tom as apposition to brother and attach yesterday to sent as a time adverbial.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: explained directly governs the result; to introduces recipient us, and clearly gives the manner, so the three parts must not be merged as one object.

exampleNotes.title: Structure focus
exampleNotes.body: with a telescope may form a postmodifier inside the object with man, or separately modify saw as an instrument; without context, both analyses remain possible.

rules: Identify the clause skeleton first, then attach modifiers, adverbials and appositives to their heads.
Use questions and substitution to test elements: who/what, does what, to whom/what, when, where and how.
For ambiguity, use meaning and phrasing to decide whether a prepositional phrase modifies a noun or verb.

questions.question: Which is the complete clause skeleton?

options.text: Subject + predicate + indirect object + direct object

questions.correct: send uses the double-object pattern here.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: send uses the double-object pattern here.

questions.question: Which question does clearly answer?
questions.correct: clearly modifies the manner of explained.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: clearly modifies the manner of explained.

questions.question: Why can with a telescope have two analyses?

options.text: It may modify man or give the instrument of saw
It can only be a time adverbial

questions.correct: Context decides between “the man who had it” and “saw by means of it”.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Context decides between “the man who had it” and “saw by means of it”.

narration.text:
综合分析不是一次给每个词贴标签，而是先抓骨架，再把说明性内容挂回它真正修饰的中心。遇到不确定，还要用提问、替换和语境验证。<#0.8#>
My brother Tom sent me a photo yesterday。<#0.8#>主干先看 sent 前后的关系：My brother Tom 是主语，me 是接收者，a photo 是被传递的东西。Tom 与 brother 指同一个人，作同位语；yesterday 再补充时间。<#0.8#>
The young scientist explained the result to us clearly。<#0.8#>explained 直接带 the result，to 把关系指向 us，clearly 回答怎样解释。直接宾语、介词宾语和方式状语要分开，不能全并成一块。<#0.8#>
She saw the man with a telescope。<#0.8#>with a telescope 可能跟 man 连在一起，说明是哪一个人；也可能修饰 saw，说明看的工具。页面没有更多语境时，两种结构都要保留。<#0.8#>
完整步骤是：找限定谓语，划主干槽位，框出短语或从句边界，把定语和状语挂回中心，最后用语义检查。无法由语境排除的歧义，不要强行只留一个答案。
